Detailed Description:
I am formally escalating a safety concern raised by American Airlines Safety Chair regarding repeated operational risk exposure at Gate C21.
Over the past couple of days, during active pushback operations on AA2496 and AA2798, roadway vehicles proceeded past aircraft while pushback was in progress. The recurring nature of these events indicates elevated exposure that warrants coordinated intervention.
Key Risk Factors Identified:
•	Visibility constraints caused by equipment staging supporting widebody operations at C23
•	Roadway curvature limiting driver sightlines and reaction time
•	Wingwalkers positioned in accordance with our ROM pushback requirements but not readily visible to roadway traffic
•	Repeated encroachment into the established aircraft safety envelope
As outlined in our JCBA, both the Company and the Union share a responsibility to cooperate fully in furthering the safety of air transportation operations . 
This concern has been formally elevated by Union safety leadership, and it is appropriate that we address it collaboratively and proactively.
I am requesting a joint safety review including:
•	American Airlines Safety and Station Leadership
•	Port of Portland Safety
•	Alaska Airlines operational leadership
•	Business partners (including McGee and Sky Chefs)
•	TWU-IAM Union Safety representation
Proposed focus areas:
•	Equipment staging boundaries at C23 during widebody operations
•	Temporary or permanent roadway speed mitigation at the end of Concourse C
•	Enhanced hazard recognition controls during pushback operations
•	Clear delineation and enforcement of safety envelope protection
We have avoided a serious event to date. The pattern, however, suggests increasing risk exposure if mitigation is not implemented.
The Leadership Team and I are available to coordinate an in-person walkthrough to review sightline staging practices, and roadway dynamics in real time.
Thank you in advance for your partnership in addressing this before an incident occurs.
Hazard Report Status: 2026-05-06: - Hazard Validated and Investigation Complete - Scheduled for Risk Assessment

Detailed Description:
At this flex gate, the safety envelope markings currently show a solid line for narrow-body aircraft and a dotted line for widebody aircraft. This setup has led to confusion among ground handlers, with some positioning equipment outside the narrow-body safety line when a widebody is expected.

This inconsistency has already resulted in damage to both an aircraft and a belt loader.

To eliminate ambiguity and improve safety, it is recommended to remove the narrow-body safety line and designate the widebody envelope as the single solid reference line. This approach ensures that all ground equipment remains clear of the largest required safety envelope, regardless of whether a narrow-body or widebody aircraft is assigned to the gate.

Implementing this change will standardize positioning practices and reduce the risk of future incidents.

Sincerely,
Danger

Detailed Description:
This morning at 0819L AF1 (Danny Gilliland) was conducting a runway inspection on runway 28R. He was cleared onto the runway by ATC and began the inspection. Approximately 1 minute later ATC cleared a Pilatus PC12 to take off on runway 28R. AF1 informed ATC he was still on the runway while simultaneously exiting at the closest taxiway, A3. ATC canceled the takeoff clearance and the PC-12 held short of the runway. It does not appear that an actual incursion occurred, but this was a serious situation that could have had tragic consequences.  

A factor that may have contributed: It appears aircraft on the same runway were using both 118.7 and 123.775. A challenger that departed prior to AF1 requesting the runway was on 118.7 the Pilatus was on 123.775. AF1 switched from 123.775 to 118.7 since the challengers was on that frequency and believed split runway frequencies were being used. ATC was simulcasting on both frequencies so they may not have been aware that AF1 and the Pilatus could not here each other.

On 118.7: AF1 requests clearance to inspect 28R from K1; file 081830DA at 00:19 (time: 0819L)

On 118.7/123.775: Tower clears AF1 onto 28R, file 081830DA at 00:24 (time: 0819L)

On 118.7/123.775: Tower clears Pilatus N726KP to take off on 28R; file 081958DA (time: 0820L)

On 118.7 AF1 informs Tower (twice) he is still on the runway; file 081958DA at 00:16 (time: 0820L)

On 118.7/123.775: Tower cancels takeoff clearance for Pilatus N726KP; file 081958DA at 00:20 (time: 0820L)

On 123.775: Pilatus N726KP acknowledges canceled take off clearance;  file 081958DA (time: 0820L)

Statement from Danny Gilliliand:

“This morning, during my inspection of RWY 10L/28R (around 0818 to 0821), the Tower controller cleared an aircraft to take off while I was on the runway.

Prior to my inspection, I monitored tower frequency 123.775 to discern if we were using combined tower frequency or if I should switch to 118.7. A departing aircraft was told by ATC to contact departure, and I did not hear it respond on 123.775, leading me to switch to 118.7 to contact tower for my inspection clearance. Tower cleared me onto the runway for inspection at roughly 0818 or 0819. While halfway down the runway, I heard the controller clear an aircraft for takeoff. I immediately broadcast my position on frequency and began heading for the exit at TWY A3. Due to no response from ATC (likely stepped on by the aircraft responding to the takeoff clearance), I broadcasted my location on the runway a second time before exiting the runway. The controller cancelled the aircraft’s takeoff clearance prior to it entering the runway and cleared me back onto the runway to continue my inspection. I had the controller confirm the instruction before acknowledging and proceeding back on.

I do not believe that any actual runway incursion occurred, but due to the nature of the incident I believe it is worth investigating.”

Although the situation was corrected quickly, this situation had the serious potential for a terrible outcome. In light of that and to avoid a reoccurrence this should be reviewed with a safety lens.
